name: Argopelter
description: A fearsome critter of North American lumberjack folklore — a slender, ape-like beast said to dwell in hollow trees of the conifer woods and to hurl branches and wood splinters at passing humans.

aliases.name: Agropelter
aliases.meaning: Original spelling used by William T. Cox (1910)

aliases.name: Anthrocephalus craniofractens
aliases.meaning: Mock-Latin binomial coined by William T. Cox

origin: Said by Cox (1910) to inhabit the coniferous forests of North America from Maine to Oregon, with the densest reporting in the Great Lakes / Upper Midwest lumber region.
